hero.h1: Basement Flooding Help in Arlington Heights, IL
hero.sub: Water on the basement floor after a storm usually comes from one of three places: the sewer, the ground or the surface. We figure out which one, fix the plumbing that let it in and help you keep it out next time. From our office on East Central Road, 24/7.

blocks.intro: The fix depends on where the water came from:

tiles.body: Sewage or storm water pushing back from the sewer. A blocked line or an overloaded sewer is the cause.
Groundwater rising around the foundation. That's a sump pump and drainage problem.
Surface water from heavy rain, clogged gutters or a yard that slopes toward the house.
A burst pipe, a failed water heater or a washer hose. Shut off the water and call.

blocks.intro: On July 23, 2011, almost 7 inches of rain fell on Arlington Heights in just over three hours. The sewers were designed for about 2.5 to 3 inches over a full day, and basements in many parts of town took on water.

items.h3: Sewer Backups Through the Floor Drain
items.body: In 2011, many homes had sewage back up through basement floor drains, and village officials pointed to overhead sewers as the main fix. That's why the floor drain matters so much here.

items.h3: Combined Sewers in the Older Part of Town
items.body: Some older neighborhoods near the center of town have combined sewers that fill with storm water in heavy rain. Gravity basement drains in those areas are the most exposed.
Areas like Westgate and Park Manor were hit in 2011, and in 2016 residents in flood-prone parts of town described repeated basement flooding. If that's you, a long-term plan is worth it.

A clear sewer line, a [sump pump with a battery backup](/arlington-heights/sump-pumps) and an [overhead sewer system](/arlington-heights/overhead-sewer-systems) cover the three main ways water gets in.

bodies: Waterproofing keeps groundwater out of the basement. The plumbing side of it is what we handle: sump pits and pumps, battery backups, discharge lines and the drain tile that carries water to the pit.

If water comes through the walls or where the wall meets the floor, the drain tile may be clogged or missing, or the sump pump can't keep up. We check the system and tell you what will actually stop the water. For water coming up through the floor drain, see [sewage backup service](/arlington-heights/sewage-line-backup-services).

blocks.h2: Basement Flooding Questions From Arlington Heights Homeowners

items.q: What should I do first when my basement floods?
items.preview: Stay safe, stop the water if you can and call.
items.answer: Keep away from water near outlets or appliances. If the water is coming from a pipe or appliance, shut off the main water valve. If it's coming up through the floor drain, stop using water in the house. Then call us.

items.q: How do I know if it's sewage or groundwater?
items.preview: Sewage comes up through drains and smells. Groundwater seeps in at the walls and floor.
items.answer: Sewage usually comes up through the floor drain, a basement toilet or a shower and has a smell. Groundwater seeps in where the walls meet the floor or through cracks and is usually clear.

items.q: Will a sump pump stop sewer backups?
items.preview: No. Sump pumps handle groundwater. Backups need a backflow valve or overhead sewer.
items.answer: No. A sump pump handles groundwater. Sewer backups need a clear line and protection like a backflow valve or an overhead sewer system.

items.q: My basement has flooded twice. What's the long-term fix?
items.preview: Find the source, then match the fix: line repair, backflow protection or a better sump system.
items.answer: First, confirm where the water comes in. Then match the fix: a sewer repair or overhead sewer for backups, a stronger sump system and battery backup for groundwater, and grading or gutter fixes for surface water. We'll put it in writing.

items.preview: It depends on the source and the fix. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on where the water is coming from and what it takes to stop it. We give you a flat-rate price for each option before any work begins.
